newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Outgoing Guinea-Bissau leader defends record.
newsitem.headline: Outgoing Guinea-Bissau leader defends record.

text.p: Guinea-Bissau Prime Minister Manuel Saturnino da Costa, whose government was dissolved by the president, denied charges the West African state had faced a crisis, the Portuguese news agency Lusa said on Tuesday.
Da Costa sent a letter to President Joao Bernardo Vieira disputing his charge in a decree on Monday dissolving the government that a serious political crisis existed in the former Portuguese colony.

Lusa, which had a copy of Da Costa's letter, reported from the capital Bissau that Vieira had said there was a "grave political crisis" jeopardising operations of state institutions. The agency gave no details of the reported crisis.
Da Costa said "certain political forces disturbed by the (positive) results of the government" were creating a "false crisis", Lusa reported.

He said the government of Guinea-Bissau, one of the world's poorest states, had brought "credibility to the country, reinforced the confidence of partners in its development and brought a climate of cooperation to civil society."
He referred to "satisfactory results" by his government in its structural adjustment programme with the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, which would improve future access to funds.

Lusa reported Da Costa's government, which took office in November 1994, would remain pending appointment of a new executive. It did not say when the new government would be sworn in or who it would include.
